The item in question is described as a flange type bearing, part number 104-8699. A sample was submitted. In your request you indicate that subject bearing is a “housed” bearing comprised of a flanged housing, thirteen steel balls each with a diameter of 3/16 of an inch, a steel center piece, and a disk shaped seal. The balls are inserted between the “housing” and the center piece, the housing is packed with grease, the disk is placed to seal the “housing” and the “housing” is then crimped to complete the assembly. The centerpiece and the “housing” provide the rolling surface for the steel balls and serve as the bearing’s inner and outer race, respectively. The “housing”, not including its flange, is approximately 1-1/8 inches in outside diameter. It is our position that for tariff purposes a bearing housing consists of a frame or block designed to house another wise complete bearing. Because the “housing” in this case is actually the outer race for and completes the flange bearing it does not house the bearing.

In your letter dated November 20, 2002 you requested a tariff classification ruling regarding a set of drinking glasses from China. The merchandise at issue is a set of four Margarita drinking glasses. You stated that the value of the set of four drinking glasses is $5.14 while the value of each drinking glass within the set is $1.29. The classification of drinking glasses (as well as other household glassware) is dependent on value. In your inquiry you asked whether a classification determination for this merchandise is based on the price of a group of drinking glasses marketed as a set or the price of a single drinking glass. For glassware classified based on value, any classification determination must be based on the value of a single glass article, not the value of several items packaged together as a set. Therefore, the classification of the drinking glasses at issue will be based on the unit value of $1.29 for a single drinking glass, not the price of $5.14 for the set of four drinking glasses.

The merchandise subject to this ruling is a voltage supply module/”camera modulator”. The voltage supply module/”camera modulator” is assembled into the entire rear view camera system of Mercedes-Benz automobiles. The voltage supply module/”camera modulator” consists of a populated printed circuit assembly. The printed circuit assembly contains various resistors, capacitors, and inductors, which are encased in a plastic housing. There are connections on the unit to plug in the camera’s cable and the cable to the car’s electrical system. The voltage supply module/”camera modulator” is a direct current to direct current (DC/DC) converter. It supplies voltage from the vehicle’s electrical system to the separate rear view camera unit and forwards and amplifies the composite video baseband signal (CVBS) signal sent from the camera to the head unit/monitor. It does not modulate the CVBS signal. The entire camera system works in the following way. When the driver engages the reverse gear, it forces a signal to be sent to switch on the exterior back-up lamps (tail lights) of the vehicle. One of the two back-up lamps sends an electrical pulse to the voltage supply module. The voltage supply module activates the camera by supplying it with voltage. As the camera captures CVBS analog images in real time, these CVBS signals are sent back to the voltage supply module, which in turn transmits the CVBS signals to the head unit for video display to the driver on the monitor of the head unit. Although the entire system contains a camera and a monitor, they are not part of the voltage supply module/”camera modulator” unit. They are a part of the entire system, as the voltage supply module/”camera modulator is. As such, the voltage supply module/”camera modulator” is a DC/DC converter that converts direct current power from the vehicle’s electrical system for further use with the rear view camera unit. Subsequently, it forwards and amplifies the CVBS signal from the camera to the head unit/monitor.

The merchandise subject to this ruling is an Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet. It is identified within your letter as Part # ER-FLY. The Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet is designed to provide immediate power and charging power for a number of devices including laptops, portable DVD players, portable gaming systems, iPod/MP3 players, cell phones, digital cameras, camcorders, etc. It is imported with a wall outlet adapter that incorporates a rectifier, which converts alternating current (AC) power to direct current (DC) power, and a cigarette outlet adapter, which converts DC power to DC power of a different voltage. The Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet itself contains a rechargeable lithium-ion battery that provides DC power when a device is plugged directly into the ER-FLY’s socket. It can also provide AC power when the DC power coming from the rechargeable lithium-ion battery is converted by its built-in inverter power circuit from DC to AC. A sample of the Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet (ER-FLY) was furnished to this office for classification purposes and is being returned to you as per your request. When stationary, the Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet can be plugged into a wall power outlet or a motor vehicle’s 12 volt cigarette outlet for a consistent source of power and/or battery recharging power. When the Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet is plugged into a wall outlet, the AC power is converted to DC power by the adapter’s built-in rectifier and the DC power is provided to the device that it is plugged into. When the Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet is plugged into a motor vehicle’s 12 volt cigarette outlet, DC power is also supplied to the device that it is plugged into providing immediate power and/or recharging power to the devices battery. When mobile, the Energizer Energi To Go® Portable Power Outlet utilizes its rechargeable lithium-ion battery to provide clean, consistent DC or AC power for mobile devices, as well as recharging capabilities.

The submitted sample is identified as a Forma Toothbrush/Toothpaste Caddy. This item is comprised of two separate components. One component is the inner toothbrush/toothpaste holder, which is made of a clear styrene-acrylonitrile (SAN) plastic material. The other component is an outer housing, which is made of stainless steel. As you requested, the sample will be returned to you. The inner holder stands 5-3/4 inches high. It has a top section which is round in shape when viewed from above and has a circumference that measures 4-1/8 inches. The top section has three oblong shaped apertures, each of which cuts through the top and bottom surfaces of this section. Of the three apertures, two of them are of equal size and are designed for the purpose of having toothbrushes inserted through them. The other aperture is a larger one and is designed for the purpose of having a toothpaste tube inserted through it. The bottom section of the holder is also round in shape when viewed from above and has a circumference that measures 3-1/16 inches. This section does not have any apertures but has a depth that measures ¾ of an inch. The bottom section is designed to receive the bottom of the toothbrushes and the toothpaste tube that are inserted through the apertures in the top section of the holder. In the center of the bottom section of the holder is a molded narrow projection or post that extends upward. The post measures 4-7/8 inches in height. The top of the post is inserted into a small aperture in the bottom surface of the top section of the holder, thereby connecting the two sections. The outer housing stands 5-1/4 inches in height and is cylindrical in shape. It is closed at the bottom and opened at the top. The circumference of the bottom of the housing is 3-1/8 inches and the circumference of the opened mouth at the top is 4-1/8 inches. The plastic inner holder is inserted through the top opened mouth of the housing so that the smaller bottom section of the inner holder sits at the bottom of the housing and the top section of the inner holder sits along the rim of the top opened mouth of the housing. There is a ridge along the outer circumference of the top section of the inner holder, which allows this section to sit on the rim of the top open mouth of the housing. This item is considered to be a composite good within the meaning of General Rule of Interpretation (GRI) 3. The inner plastic holder acts as the caddy. The apertures of the plastic holder provide separate locations for toothbrushes and the toothpaste tube. This holder can actually stand by itself, without the stainless steel housing and can perform the intended function without that housing. The stainless steel housing serves the subordinate role of providing support for the plastic holder, as well as providing visual appeal. Therefore, it is the opinion of this office that the plastic holder provides this item with the essential character within the meaning of GRI 3(b).
